title: Instance Facet
description: Binds an AUTHORED atom to the template slot it fills. Single-writer: the ALSAP Lead (via the Amanuensis authoring loop) — NOT the headwater agent, which owns the form facet on a template drop. The writer boundary is why this is its own facet rather than an extension of form: two writers on one facet breaks single-writer. An authored instance is a SPARSE OVERLAY over a pinned template — controlled standard text is never copied down, it resolves from the template at render time — so an instance atom exists only where there is genuinely new meaning to embed. An atom carrying this facet carries no form or procedure facet: it is not a template node. Staleness is free: a template revision changes that template atom's content_hash, and one walk over template_source_hash names every instance that has gone stale and exactly where.

instantiates.description: atom_id of the TEMPLATE atom this value fills. Resolved against the template store named by the instance manifest's instantiates_template, not against this store. This is a persisted cross-store reference, and it is legal because it points UP into a governed shared tier — the same direction as role_ / rec_ / doc_ / reg_ registry ids. Sideways (peer project to peer project) and downward (shared to instance) remain forbidden.

fills_slot.description: Which NAMED slot inside the template atom's source_text this value fills, when the template atom is standard text carrying [bracketed] authorable spans (form.constraints.slots). Omitted when the instance fills the whole field. Together with instantiates this is the compound stable key (atom_id, slot_id) — never positional, because a position in a string shifts the moment anyone edits the sentence. Its presence is also what makes an instance atom legal over controlled_standard text: the sentence is retained, only the declared slot is authored.

template_document.description: docs.registry id (doc_...) of the controlled template document this instance is written against. The human-legible half of the pin; instantiates is the machine half.

template_version.description: The template document version this value was authored against, as document control states it (e.g. '1.0'). Pinned, not tracked: an instance is authored against a specific approved template and does not silently follow it forward.

template_source_hash.description: The template atom's content_hash at the moment this value was authored. If it no longer matches the template atom's current hash, the template's MEANING moved underneath this instance and the value is stale — the same source_hash discipline every facet owner already follows, applied across the template/instance boundary.

disposition_decision.description: Recorded here ONLY when the decision produced an atom — i.e. 'modified'. Decisions that produce no new meaning (retained / marked_not_applicable / deleted) have no atom to ride on and live in the external instance_decisions.json instead. MIRROR of vocab/instance.enum.json disposition_decision ids.

selected_value.description: For a template slot whose field_type is select_one/select_many, the governed value id chosen from the set behind the template's options_ref. Held as an id, never as the option's prose: the label and definition live once, in the options registry. The gate checks it against that set — this is where 'select one of the six governed values and never invent a seventh' is actually enforced.

authored_by.description: roles.registry id (role_...) accountable for this value. A ROLE, never a person — no PII in content, on the instance side exactly as on the template side.

proposed_by_agent.description: Identifier of the authoring agent whose proposal a human accepted to produce this value (e.g. 'amanuensis'). Provenance, not authority: the agent writes nothing, and acceptance plus the gates are what make a value canon. Absent when a human authored it unaided.
